title: Spielerando: The Game Workbench for Vibe Coding
excerpt: The companion workbench for vibe coding games: blueprints, tested code, story and rule checks, and project files in versions for Claude Code, Cursor and any coding AI.

What do you want to build?

Learn it in the order that works

A tree sorts, a path leads. Each path is a handful of steps in an order that works, with the reason every step comes where it does. Your AI can follow them too.

How it works

Find your topic

A few of the entries

Each one with steps, values, pitfalls and tested code for your AI.

My boss is supposed to have three phases but sometimes skips one

A boss that changes at certain health levels can jump straight over a phase when one big hit crosses two of them, and a typo in the list can make a phase unreachable. This helper checks the list and tells you which phase is at risk and which one applies at any health.

Letter-guess colors are wrong when a word has the same letter twice

Your word game marks a letter as present although the secret word has no more of it, and players call it a lie. Two passes over the guess fix it, and the order of those passes is the part that most AI drafts get backwards.

Let players buy ten upgrades at once when each one costs more

In a clicker, every machine you build costs a bit more than the last, and players want a "buy as many as I can" button. A shortcut formula tells them they can afford one more than the shop will actually sell. This entry makes the button and the price shown agree to the last coin.

A line greets the player by name, but on one route the name was never asked

Stories remember things like a name, a gift or a promise, and later lines use them. If one road to that line skips the moment where the thing was set, the text shows a hole. This entry checks every road, not just the one you tested.

Tap for a short hop, hold for a high jump

Letting go early should make a lower jump, yet most first attempts feel like hitting an invisible ceiling or make small jumps feel mushy. Here is the moment and the way to cut the jump so it feels natural, with numbers to start from.

A player swaps the offer at the last moment of a trade

Both players press accept, but one of them changed what was on the table a heartbeat before, and the other agrees to a deal they never saw. Here is how a trade window stays honest even when the connection is slow.
